scope_note: Models coding and unit-debug effort only. Excludes deployment, CI, board bring-up, assurance-case authoring, requirements elicitation meetings, and team coordination overheads.

c_infra.rationale: Hand-written seL4/Microkit C bridge, queue, and FFI code: low-level, shared-memory, concurrency-sensitive; embedded-C productivity literature supports single-digit SLOC/h for this class.

rust_infra.rationale: Hand-written Rust port APIs, FFI bindings, and crate wiring for a no_std target; systems-Rust rate placeholder.

rust_contract_woven.rationale: Verus contract clauses (requires/ensures) hand-authored on entry points; formal-specification authoring is slow per line.

rust_app_code.rationale: Application entry-point logic against a typed port API; ordinary verified-application Rust.

rust_test_code.rationale: Hand-written unit/contract/property test bodies; tests are faster per line than product code.

rust_test_infra.rationale: Test harness plumbing (port put/get shims, oracle wiring, generators) a manual path would hand-build.

c_user_code.rationale: C-to-Rust user bridge shims; mechanical but FFI-sensitive.

microkit_config.rationale: Microkit system XML (protection domains, memory regions, channels) and schedule slots: dense, error-prone platform configuration.

gumbo_contract.rationale: GUMBO state/integration/initialize/compute clauses: formal contract authoring rate.

sysml_model.rationale: SysMLv2 architecture and data modeling in the HAMR subset.

requirements_text.rationale: ConOps/requirements prose and tables with stable IDs; lines-of-prose is a weak proxy — see requirement_items counts for a future per-item rate.

build_script.rationale: bin/build.cmd is generated by the setup-build-script skill, which a non-agentic HAMR user also has; modeled as a fixed setup activity (fixed_hours_override), not hand-written SLOC. The SLOC rate is retained only for a manual-path sensitivity discussion. Conservative: understates human effort on the HAMR path.

makefile.rationale: Build rules for cross-compiled Microkit images; mostly patterned but fragile.

build_config.rationale: Cargo manifests and toolchain pins; mechanical.

proof_code.rationale: Verus system-proof code (state machines, VCs, lemmas): formal-methods authoring rate; seL4 proof-effort literature is the extreme upper bound.

experienced_sel4.rationale: Senior engineer already fluent in seL4/Microkit, Rust, and formal specification.

new_to_sel4.rationale: Competent engineer new to seL4/Microkit and formal contracts. Multiplier magnitudes follow COCOMO-II experience drivers (AEXP/PLEX/LTEX each ~1.4-1.6x, compounding to 2-4x on platform- and formalism-specific work).

nominal.note: A manual build writes an equivalent of every generated line.

conservative.note: A hand-built system may need only about half the generated line count (less generality, fewer harness layers).

activity_overheads.note: Fixed hours a human would spend running tools and triaging results on the HAMR path; applied per step when the step is recorded done in workflow-status. Uncalibrated placeholders.

steps.activity: run sireum tipe and fix trivial findings
run Logika integration check and record vacuity/handshakes
configure and run codegen; inspect output tree and report
generate the build script via the setup-build-script skill and verify usage
run tests with coverage instrumentation and read reports
run Verus verification and triage results
review and adjust the candidate static schedule
run the system-proof crate through Verus and triage results
